diagnosis.summary: Telegram action rejected due to invalid channel username, requiring destination/input correction.
alternate_explanations: Destination channel name might be incorrectly configured or malformed in recipient input mapping.

proposal.summary: Request manual fix of the recipient channel configuration or input mapping by the owner.
reasons: The provider rejected the request with 'Invalid channel username', which is a customer-controlled configuration or destination issue.
Invalid destination format supports a bounded owner configuration repair.
preconditions: Ensure recipient mapping matches correct format

diagnosis.summary: Telegram delivery rejected with 'Invalid channel username', pointing to an invalid destination format or incorrect channel configuration.
alternate_explanations: Bot permissions in the target channel might be misconfigured.

proposal.summary: Verify and correct the channel username or recipient destination configuration.
reasons: The provider rejected the request due to an invalid channel username.
Customer-controlled destination configuration requires manual correction.
preconditions: Ensure the channel username is valid and the bot has proper access.

diagnosis.summary: Provider response was lost after request transmission, leaving delivery status unknown and requiring abstention due to insufficient delivery evidence.
alternate_explanations: The provider may have successfully processed the request despite the lost response receipt.

proposal.summary: Abstain from replay or definitive delivery conclusions due to unknown provider response and missing historical delivery evidence.
reasons: Delivery outcome is explicitly unknown because the provider response was lost after transmission and required evidence is missing.
preconditions: Confirm independent provider side-effects or logs before attempting any further classification.

diagnosis.summary: Provider response was lost after request transmission, and delivery outcome remains unknown.
alternate_explanations: The message may have reached the provider successfully despite the lost response receipt.

proposal.summary: Delivery outcome is unknown due to lost provider response, requiring escalation.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and provider response was lost.
Required evidence items are missing to establish safe replay or definitive delivery.
preconditions: Obtain independent provider evidence or missing delivery receipts before any further action.

agentReview.reviewer: Codex agent; not independent human validation
agentReview.method: Reviewed shuffled saved-output packets before opening the mapping. Variant names hidden; case evidence and passages visible for entailment checks. Contexts/citations and prior experimental knowledge can reveal variants, so this is partial masking, not an independent blinded trial. No judge generation used.

assessments.label: pair-1-A
assessments.supportedCausalClaims: Recorded Telegram rejection and generic resolver error are supported. Invalid destination format or incorrect configuration as the cause is not established: destination validity, bot permissions and provider status are unavailable.
assessments.uncertainty: Medium confidence and a possible bot-permissions alternate are more cautious than the partner, but the correction proposal still asserts an unproven configuration defect. Listing unavailable evidence does not qualify that causal claim.
assessments.proceduralGuidance: Checking destination validity and operator-confirmed bot access is useful. Requiring correction rather than investigation is premature.
assessments.citationEntailment: The cited read-only-investigation section supports input validation and an operator confirming bot membership/permissions. It does not establish that customer configuration is defective or needs correction.
assessments.semanticQuality: Unsupported causal/remediation claim remains despite relevant guidance.

assessments.label: pair-1-B
assessments.supportedCausalClaims: The final error text and rejection are recorded; claiming a customer-controlled configuration/destination issue requiring correction overinterprets a generic resolver error.
assessments.uncertainty: High confidence is excessive for the asserted configuration cause; the alternate also stays within configuration and misses permissions uncertainty.
assessments.proceduralGuidance: Verify destination validity/mapping is a useful investigation step, but manual correction is not supported by observed inputs, which are unavailable.
assessments.citationEntailment: The cited replay-and-approval section describes restrictions on repeating invalid inputs; it does not prove inputs are invalid in this incident or entail the repair claim. The proposal includes an evidence reference fixture:failure: that does not identify a supplied evidence object.
assessments.semanticQuality: Unsupported causal/remediation claim, excessive confidence, and invalid evidence reference.

assessments.label: pair-2-A
assessments.supportedCausalClaims: Transmission and lost response are recorded; no delivery or non-delivery claim is made. Possible successful delivery is explicitly an alternate.
assessments.uncertainty: Appropriate outcome_unknown disposition and abstention. High confidence describes the known ambiguity, not successful or failed delivery.
assessments.proceduralGuidance: Escalation and seeking independent provider evidence/receipts are useful. Before any further action is slightly broad because authorized read-only investigation remains useful.
assessments.citationEntailment: The cited read-only-investigation section directly supports treating missing receipts as unknown until independent evidence resolves them.
assessments.semanticQuality: Supported bounded diagnosis with useful investigation direction.

assessments.label: pair-2-B
assessments.supportedCausalClaims: Unknown delivery after lost response is grounded in observed transmission and missing response. Successful processing remains only a possibility.
assessments.uncertainty: Appropriate abstention and outcome_unknown; no definitive delivery conclusion.
assessments.proceduralGuidance: Explicitly abstaining from replay is useful. Independent side-effects/logs are appropriate operator evidence, but requiring them before any further classification is overbroad: F07 is already supported. The partner more directly requests receipts.
assessments.citationEntailment: Read-only-investigation supports independent evidence; forbidden-actions supports refusing Telegram resend. Neither fabricates runtime receipts or authority.
assessments.semanticQuality: Supported bounded diagnosis; added prohibition citation, no clear material semantic improvement over partner.

caseComparisons.baseline: High-confidence unsupported configuration diagnosis; invalid evidence ref; service rejected.
caseComparisons.oracle: Medium-confidence configuration diagnosis, adds possible bot-permissions alternate and access check; service accepted but still wrongly implies required destination correction.
caseComparisons.conclusion: Narrow qualitative uncertainty/procedure improvement, unsupported causal claim persists. Deterministic service acceptance is not semantic validation.
caseComparisons.regression: No clear new semantic regression; persistent cause/remediation overreach in both.

caseComparisons.baseline: Correct F07/outcome_unknown/abstention, independent provider evidence or receipts requested; citation supports unknown delivery.
caseComparisons.oracle: Correct F07/outcome_unknown/abstention; explicitly refuses replay and cites forbidden-actions as well as read-only investigation.
caseComparisons.conclusion: Comparable useful diagnoses; marginal prohibition/citation detail, no clear material gain.
caseComparisons.regression: Minor procedural overconstraint: oracle asks for independent logs before further classification, though F07 is already justified. Baseline more directly asks for receipts; baseline also overbroad before any further action.

conclusion: This pilot offers a weak, mixed qualitative signal that relevant retrieval can improve uncertainty and procedural/citation detail, but does not demonstrate reliable improvement in causal diagnosis. The retrieval-limited ambiguous case remains unsupported even with the reviewed oracle.
limitation: Two development cases and one repetition cannot establish reliable improvement or justify production adoption. Review is by the same implementation agent, not independent human validation; partial variant masking cannot remove prior knowledge. Sampling variation and order remain confounders.
